description: Be ready to cook something great...
summary: BurnWindow is a web application that turns NASA MODIS and VIIRS hotspot records into an understandable burning-activity calendar. Users search a place, compare satellite observations, explore seasonal patterns, and inspect locally calibrated estimates with their errors. Plain-language summaries explain what each result means, while missing observations remain visibly unknown. Our evidence workbench combines native cloud/swath checks, independently mapped fire events, and a frozen geographic evaluation. The application helps researchers and land managers investigate historical burning without confusing changes in satellite sensitivity with changes in fire activity. Its contribution is an inspectable, reproducible comparison that exposes uncertainty and model failures alongside useful historical context.
details:
BurnWindow addresses the challenge of comparing fire observations collected by satellites with different resolutions, sensitivities and observation times.

The application converts eligible reports into common spatial cells and UTC days, preserving separate satellite and day/night records. Local annual and seasonal calibration factors are fitted on earlier years and evaluated against later Aqua observations. Interactive calendars, historical comparisons, uncertainty diagnostics and plain-language explanations help users investigate patterns and unusual months.

The bundled application contains approximately 1.5 million NASA records and supports worldwide place lookup, coordinate selection and additional country-archive imports. Its validation workbench includes nine paired NASA fire-mask/geolocation granules, corroboration against 23 independently mapped MTBS events, and 16 frozen geographic evaluation cases.

These studies establish bounded evidence, not universal accuracy. Geographic testing exposed substantial nighttime transfer errors; Aqua is a comparator rather than ground truth, and observation coverage remains unknown outside the registered mask studies.

Built with Python, SQLite, JavaScript, HTML and CSS, BurnWindow provides source hashes, downloadable evidence and reproducible evaluation commands. Its creative contribution is connecting each result to an explanation of its meaning, supporting evidence and limitations. The intended impact is more informed historical fire analysis, rather than an operational emergency-warning claim.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS — MODIS and VIIRS active-fire records
projectRefs: NOAA JPSS public data — operational fire masks and geolocation
USGS/USFS MTBS — independently mapped fire perimeters
